expected_answer: Theft is punishable by imprisonment and/or a fine. Simple theft carries a penalty of imprisonment for a period not exceeding two years and/or a fine. Aggravated theft (e.g., at night, with weapons, from a dwelling) can result in imprisonment for up to seven years.

Workers who have completed one year of service are entitled to annual leave of 30 days per year. During the probation period, workers accrue leave at 2 days per month. Leave is fully paid based on the basic salary.

Unauthorized access to electronic systems, websites, or information networks is punishable by imprisonment and/or a fine not less than AED 100,000 and not exceeding AED 300,000. If the access results in data destruction or alteration, penalties are more severe.

Child custody is determined based on the best interest of the child. The mother generally has priority for custody of young children (boys up to age 11, girls up to age 13). The court considers the custodian's ability to provide proper care, education, and a stable environment.

A valid contract under UAE civil law requires: mutual consent of the parties, a lawful subject matter, a cause or purpose that is not contrary to public order or morals, and legal capacity of the contracting parties.

Premeditated murder is punishable by the death penalty or life imprisonment. Intentional killing without premeditation carries imprisonment for a period not less than five years and up to fifteen years.

End-of-service gratuity is calculated as: 21 days of basic salary for each year of the first five years of service, and 30 days of basic salary for each additional year. The total gratuity shall not exceed two years' salary.
The probation period shall not exceed six months from the date of commencing work. The employer may terminate the worker during probation with 14 days' written notice.

Yes, defamation is a criminal offense in the UAE. It is punishable by imprisonment for up to two years and/or a fine not exceeding AED 500,000. This includes spoken, written, or electronic defamation.

Grounds for divorce include: mutual consent, harm or discord, failure to maintain the spouse, absence of the husband for more than one year, imprisonment of the spouse for three or more years, and incurable defect or disease.

An employer may not terminate a worker without notice except in cases of gross misconduct. Otherwise, at least 30 days' written notice is required. Termination without proper notice entitles the worker to compensation in lieu of notice.
Online fraud is punishable by imprisonment for a period not less than one year and a fine not less than AED 250,000 and not exceeding AED 1,000,000, or either penalty.

Compensation includes both actual damage suffered (direct loss) and lost profit, provided the damage is a natural result of the harmful act. The court determines the amount based on the circumstances.

Normal working hours shall not exceed eight hours per day or 48 hours per week. Overtime is compensated at 125% of normal pay for daytime overtime and 150% for nighttime overtime (between 10 PM and 4 AM). During Ramadan, working hours are reduced by two hours.

Inheritance follows Islamic Sharia principles for Muslim UAE nationals. The estate is distributed after deducting funeral expenses, debts, and bequests (up to one-third). Male heirs generally receive double the share of female heirs of the same degree.

Yes, sharing someone's private photos without their consent is illegal under UAE cybercrime law. It is punishable by imprisonment for at least six months and/or a fine between AED 150,000 and AED 500,000.

UAE labour law prohibits discrimination based on race, color, sex, religion, national origin, or disability. Employers must provide equal pay for equal work. Harassment in the workplace is also prohibited and can result in penalties.

Drug possession for personal use may result in a minimum of two years imprisonment, rehabilitation, or deportation for non-nationals. Trafficking carries much harsher penalties including life imprisonment or the death penalty for large quantities.

Under penal law, assault is punishable by imprisonment. Under labour law, the worker can file a complaint with the Ministry of Human Resources and may terminate the contract with full entitlements if the employer or their representative assaults the worker.

Theft involves taking someone's property without their knowledge or consent. Robbery involves taking property using force, violence, or threats. Robbery carries significantly harsher penalties than simple theft.

Kidnapping is punishable by imprisonment. If the victim is a minor, the penalty is increased. If force, threats, or deception are used, the perpetrator faces imprisonment for a period not less than five years.
Workers are entitled to sick leave of up to 90 days per year: the first 15 days at full pay, the next 30 days at half pay, and any remaining days without pay.

Cybercrimes include unauthorized access to electronic systems, data theft, online fraud, identity theft, publishing defamatory content online, invasion of privacy, creating or distributing illegal content, and using technology for terrorist purposes.

The mother has priority for custody of young children (boys until 11, girls until 13). She must be of sound mind, trustworthy, and capable of raising the child. The mother loses custody rights if she remarries someone not related to the child.

Yes, during the probation period, the employer may terminate the worker with 14 days' written notice. The worker may also resign during probation with 14 days' notice (or 30 days if moving to another UAE employer).

Forgery of official documents is punishable by imprisonment for a period not less than one year and not exceeding five years. Forgery of non-official documents carries a lesser penalty of up to two years.

Property ownership transfers through valid contract, inheritance, or legal decree. The transfer must be registered with the relevant authority. Both movable and immovable property are governed by specific provisions.

Yes, gambling is illegal in the UAE. Any person who gambles in a public place shall be punished by imprisonment and/or a fine. Operating or managing a gambling establishment carries a harsher penalty.
This question is outside the scope of UAE legal knowledge. The system should indicate it cannot answer non-legal questions.

If an employer fails to pay wages on time, the worker may file a complaint with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The employer may face penalties and fines. Repeated failure can lead to suspension of the establishment's work permits.
